newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean automakers hit Samsung in war over report.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean automakers hit Samsung in war over report.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co and five other South Korean automakers said on Monday the Samsung Group must give up its bid to make cars if a restructuring of the industry was inevitable.
The six automakers also declared joint action against Samsung over a war sparked by Samsung's report that the local auto industry needed restructuring.

"If restructuring was inevitable due to oversupply, it is desirable for Samsung Motors Inc which has never made cars and has no experience and independent technology to give up its business," the statement said.

The statement was jointly issued by chief executives of the Korea Automobile Manufacturers Association, Hyundai Motor, Kia Motors Corp, Daewoo Motor Co, Asia Motors Co, Ssangyong Motor Co and Hyundai Precision and Industry Co.
The automakers' association is headed by Hyundai Motor Co's chief executive officer and chairman Chung Mong-gyu.
The statement also asked the government to closely watch the progress of Samsung's carmaking project to ensure that Samsung abides by its own promises put forward in 1994.
It was referring to Samsung's promises that it would not interfere with the flow of parts to existing automakers and that it would not recruit workers from existing makers.

In 1994 Samsung won a government license to enter the car industry in a technical tie-up with Japan's Nissan Motor Co. Samsung plans to make 80,000 vehicles in 1998, with the output rising to 250,000 in 1999 and 500,000 by 2002.

The South Korean automobile industry has been rocked by Samsung's internal report, which proposed restructuring the local car industry to overcome a possible crisis in the sector following excessive facilities investment and an oversupply.
Samsung officials have acknowledged the existence of a report, but have declined to officially comment.
